messages.content: I want to use auto-bot. What is it?
The auto-bot module — Autonomous task bot: gather, craft, build, farm and more. It is in the Log Client category and has 25 settings.
Which settings should I look at first?

The ones with the most effect are `auto-start`, `pause-on-disconnect`, `task-timeout`. `auto-start` — Start working as soon as an objective is added. `pause-on-disconnect` — Pause the bot when the world changes or the connection drops. `task-timeout` — Seconds a single task may run before it is failed.
How do I turn it on?
Open the window with `!log gui` and switch on auto-bot, or send POST /api/v1/modules/auto-bot with {"active": true} to the companion API. Run `log modules` to confirm it is on.
I want to use chat-digest. What is it?
The chat-digest module — Summarises chat activity on demand and on a timer. It is in the Log Client category and has 5 settings.
Which settings should I look at first?

The ones with the most effect are `automatic`, `interval-minutes`, `window-size`. `automatic` — Print a digest automatically on a timer. `interval-minutes` — Minutes between automatic digests. `window-size` — How many recent messages a digest covers.
How do I turn it on?
Open the window with `!log gui` and switch on chat-digest, or send POST /api/v1/modules/chat-digest with {"active": true} to the companion API. Run `log modules` to confirm it is on.
I want to use chat-filter. What is it?
The chat-filter module — Suppresses chat noise with ordered hide/allow rules. It is in the Log Client category and has 3 settings.
Which settings should I look at first?

The ones with the most effect are `rules`, `default-action`, `announce-hides`. `rules` — Filter rules, one per line, applied top to bottom. First match wins. `default-action` — What to do with a message no rule matches. `announce-hides` — Print a chat note the first time a rule hides a message.
How do I turn it on?
Open the window with `!log gui` and switch on chat-filter, or send POST /api/v1/modules/chat-filter with {"active": true} to the companion API. Run `log modules` to confirm it is on.
I want to use chat-logger. What is it?
The chat-logger module — Records chat to disk for search, export and stats. It is in the Log Client category and has 27 settings.
Which settings should I look at first?

The ones with the most effect are `recording`, `chat-feedback`, `duplicate-detection`. `recording` — Record incoming chat to disk. `chat-feedback` — Print recording status changes to chat. `duplicate-detection` — Ignore a line that repeats the same sender and text within the window.
How do I turn it on?
Open the window with `!log gui` and switch on chat-logger, or send POST /api/v1/modules/chat-logger with {"active": true} to the companion API. Run `log modules` to confirm it is on.
I want to use chat-monitor. What is it?
The chat-monitor module — Live chat feed with search, filters and highlighting. It is in the Log Client category and has 10 settings.
Which settings should I look at first?

The ones with the most effect are `feed-size`, `show-timestamps`, `show-sender`. `feed-size` — How many recent messages the live feed keeps. `show-timestamps` — Prefix each live message with its time. `show-sender` — Prefix each live message with the sender name.
How do I turn it on?
Open the window with `!log gui` and switch on chat-monitor, or send POST /api/v1/modules/chat-monitor with {"active": true} to the companion API. Run `log modules` to confirm it is on.
I want to use chat-timestamps. What is it?
The chat-timestamps module — Prefixes incoming chat with the time it arrived. It is in the Log Client category and has 2 settings.
Which settings should I look at first?
The ones with the most effect are `style`, `dim`. `style` — How much of the clock to show. `dim` — Draw the prefix in dark grey so the message stays the brightest part of the line.
How do I turn it on?
Open the window with `!log gui` and switch on chat-timestamps, or send POST /api/v1/modules/chat-timestamps with {"active": true} to the companion API. Run `log modules` to confirm it is on.
I want to use companion. What is it?
The companion module — Serve a small web dashboard so a phone or another machine can watch and control this client. It is in the Log Client category and has 8 settings.
Which settings should I look at first?

The ones with the most effect are `port`, `node-name`, `allow-remote`. `port` — The TCP port the companion listens on. `node-name` — The name this client shows up as in the app. `allow-remote` — Also listen on other interfaces. Anyone who can reach the port and knows the token can control this client.
How do I turn it on?
Open the window with `!log gui` and switch on companion, or send POST /api/v1/modules/companion with {"active": true} to the companion API. Run `log modules` to confirm it is on.
I want to use keyword-alerts. What is it?
The keyword-alerts module — Alerts on configurable keywords with sound and webhook options. It is in the Log Client category and has 8 settings.
Which settings should I look at first?

The ones with the most effect are `rules`, `chat-feedback`, `cooldown-seconds`. `rules` — Keyword rules, one per line: pattern;case=;whole=;sound=;webhook=;enabled=;color= `chat-feedback` — Print a chat note when a keyword matches. `cooldown-seconds` — Shortest gap between two alerts for the same rule. Matches inside the gap are counted and reported with the next alert instead of printing a line each.
How do I turn it on?
Open the window with `!log gui` and switch on keyword-alerts, or send POST /api/v1/modules/keyword-alerts with {"active": true} to the companion API. Run `log modules` to confirm it is on.
I want to use mention-alerts. What is it?
The mention-alerts module — Alerts when your name or a watched name is used in chat. It is in the Log Client category and has 9 settings.
Which settings should I look at first?

The ones with the most effect are `names`, `include-own-name`, `others-only`. `names` — Names to watch, one per line. Your own name is added automatically. `include-own-name` — Also alert when your own player name is mentioned. `others-only` — Ignore lines you sent yourself.
How do I turn it on?
Open the window with `!log gui` and switch on mention-alerts, or send POST /api/v1/modules/mention-alerts with {"active": true} to the companion API. Run `log modules` to confirm it is on.
I want to use notifications. What is it?
The notifications module — Central notification stream: chat, sound and history for every Log Client feature. It is in the Log Client category and has 6 settings.
Which settings should I look at first?

The ones with the most effect are `chat-feedback`, `chat-min-priority`, `sound`. `chat-feedback` — Print accepted notifications to chat. Off by default: the modules that raise a notification usually print it themselves, and enabling both would double it. `chat-min-priority` — Only print notifications at or above this priority to chat. `sound` — Play a sound for notifications at or above the sound priority.
How do I turn it on?
Open the window with `!log gui` and switch on notifications, or send POST /api/v1/modules/notifications with {"active": true} to the companion API. Run `log modules` to confirm it is on.
I want to use player-activity. What is it?
The player-activity module — Tracks and displays per-player chat activity. It is in the Log Client category and has 4 settings.
Which settings should I look at first?

The ones with the most effect are `rebuild-on-activate`, `min-messages`, `max-players`. `rebuild-on-activate` — Rebuild the player index from stored logs when the module is enabled. `min-messages` — Hide players below this message count in the overview. `max-players` — How many players to keep in the session summary. 0 keeps every player.
How do I turn it on?
Open the window with `!log gui` and switch on player-activity, or send POST /api/v1/modules/player-activity with {"active": true} to the companion API. Run `log modules` to confirm it is on.
I want to use player-identity. What is it?
The player-identity module — Tracks observed player name changes and a per-account watchlist. It is in the Log Client category and has 5 settings.
Which settings should I look at first?

The ones with the most effect are `track-identities`, `max-accounts`, `notify-renames`. `track-identities` — Record the names each account is seen using. `max-accounts` — How many accounts to remember. 0 keeps every account. `notify-renames` — Raise a notification when an account is seen under a new name.
How do I turn it on?
Open the window with `!log gui` and switch on player-identity, or send POST /api/v1/modules/player-identity with {"active": true} to the companion API. Run `log modules` to confirm it is on.
I want to use player-notes. What is it?
The player-notes module — Keeps notes about players and links them to observed activity. It is in the Log Client category and has 4 settings.
Which settings should I look at first?

The ones with the most effect are `notes`, `max-notes`, `chat-feedback`. `notes` — Saved notes, managed from the Notes screen. Editing this by hand is not recommended. `max-notes` — How many player notes to keep. 0 keeps every note. `chat-feedback` — Print a chat note when a note is saved or removed.
How do I turn it on?
Open the window with `!log gui` and switch on player-notes, or send POST /api/v1/modules/player-notes with {"active": true} to the companion API. Run `log modules` to confirm it is on.
I want to use repeat-collapse. What is it?
The repeat-collapse module — Hides repeated identical chat lines and reports how many times one repeated. It is in the Log Client category and has 3 settings.
Which settings should I look at first?

The ones with the most effect are `window`, `announce-count`, `ignore-own`. `window` — How soon the same line must arrive to count as a repeat, in milliseconds. `announce-count` — Print how many times a line was repeated once the run ends. `ignore-own` — Do not collapse your own messages, so a macro you are testing stays visible.
How do I turn it on?
Open the window with `!log gui` and switch on repeat-collapse, or send POST /api/v1/modules/repeat-collapse with {"active": true} to the companion API. Run `log modules` to confirm it is on.
I want to use schematic-dropper. What is it?
The schematic-dropper module — Automated schematic material dropping. It is in the Log Client category and has 43 settings.
Which settings should I look at first?

The ones with the most effect are `auto-continue`, `operation-delay`, `retry-limit`. `auto-continue` — Keep dropping until every required material has been processed. `operation-delay` — Milliseconds to wait between two drop operations. `retry-limit` — How many times a failed operation is retried before the material is skipped.
How do I turn it on?
Open the window with `!log gui` and switch on schematic-dropper, or send POST /api/v1/modules/schematic-dropper with {"active": true} to the companion API. Run `log modules` to confirm it is on.
I want to use session-history. What is it?
The session-history module — Keeps a browsable history of past recording sessions. It is in the Log Client category and has 1 settings.
Which settings should I look at first?
The ones with the most effect are `history-size`. `history-size` — How many past sessions to keep. 0 keeps every session.
How do I turn it on?
Open the window with `!log gui` and switch on session-history, or send POST /api/v1/modules/session-history with {"active": true} to the companion API. Run `log modules` to confirm it is on.
I want to use session-stats. What is it?
The session-stats module — Collects session statistics for the stats HUD and dashboard. It is in the Log Client category and has 1 settings.
Which settings should I look at first?
The ones with the most effect are `summary-on-leave`. `summary-on-leave` — Print a short session summary when leaving a world.
How do I turn it on?
Open the window with `!log gui` and switch on session-stats, or send POST /api/v1/modules/session-stats with {"active": true} to the companion API. Run `log modules` to confirm it is on.
I want to use session-timeline. What is it?
The session-timeline module — Chronological record of joins, leaves, deaths and session events. It is in the Log Client category and has 4 settings.
Which settings should I look at first?

The ones with the most effect are `record-joins`, `record-leaves`, `record-deaths`. `record-joins` — Record player joins on the timeline. `record-leaves` — Record player leaves on the timeline. `record-deaths` — Record deaths on the timeline.
How do I turn it on?
Open the window with `!log gui` and switch on session-timeline, or send POST /api/v1/modules/session-timeline with {"active": true} to the companion API. Run `log modules` to confirm it is on.
I want to use updates. What is it?
The updates module — Checks GitHub Releases for a newer build and downloads it on request. It is in the Log Client category and has 5 settings.
Which settings should I look at first?

The ones with the most effect are `channel`, `check-on-join`, `auto-download`. `channel` — Stable only offers full releases; Beta also offers pre-releases. `check-on-join` — Check for updates once after joining a world. `auto-download` — Download a newer release automatically when one is found.
How do I turn it on?
Open the window with `!log gui` and switch on updates, or send POST /api/v1/modules/updates with {"active": true} to the companion API. Run `log modules` to confirm it is on.
I want to use webhook-monitor. What is it?
The webhook-monitor module — Monitors webhook delivery health, queue depth and failure reasons. It is in the Log Client category and has 3 settings.
Which settings should I look at first?

The ones with the most effect are `notify-on-failure`, `notify-on-recovery`, `history-size`. `notify-on-failure` — Print a chat note when a webhook delivery fails. `notify-on-recovery` — Print a chat note when a delivery succeeds after a failure. `history-size` — How many delivery attempts to keep in the history. 0 keeps every attempt.
How do I turn it on?
Open the window with `!log gui` and switch on webhook-monitor, or send POST /api/v1/modules/webhook-monitor with {"active": true} to the companion API. Run `log modules` to confirm it is on.
I want to use webhook-relay. What is it?
The webhook-relay module — One webhook, rich embed output, and cards for sessions, renames and watchlist activity. It is in the Log Client category and has 24 settings.
Which settings should I look at first?

The ones with the most effect are `webhook-url`, `webhook-username`, `relay-enabled`. `webhook-url` — Discord webhook URL. Treated as a secret: never written to logs or payloads. `webhook-username` — Display name used for webhook messages. `relay-enabled` — Actually send embeds. Off means the URL is stored but nothing is transmitted.
How do I turn it on?
Open the window with `!log gui` and switch on webhook-relay, or send POST /api/v1/modules/webhook-relay with {"active": true} to the companion API. Run `log modules` to confirm it is on.
I want to use world-intelligence. What is it?
The world-intelligence module — Remembers discovered locations, biomes, resources and chunks, per world. It is in the Log Client category and has 9 settings.
Which settings should I look at first?

The ones with the most effect are `track-chunks`, `track-biomes`, `mark-spawn`. `track-chunks` — Record the chunks you visit, so the map can show where you have been. `track-biomes` — Record each biome you stand in and count how often you see it. `mark-spawn` — Mark the world spawn as a waypoint the first time you see it.
How do I turn it on?
Open the window with `!log gui` and switch on world-intelligence, or send POST /api/v1/modules/world-intelligence with {"active": true} to the companion API. Run `log modules` to confirm it is on.
I want my chat to show up in Discord. Where do I start?
Use the webhook relay. Create a webhook in the Discord channel, copy its URL, then paste it into the relay's webhook-url setting. Nothing is sent until that URL is set.
What happens if Discord is down when a message is sent?
The delivery is queued and retried. Network errors, 5xx and 429 are retried with a backoff; a 4xx is not, because a rejected payload will not become valid on a retry.
How do I check it works?
Run `log webhook test`. It sends a test card and reports the result. `log webhook preview` shows the card in game first, without sending anything.
Can different keywords go to different channels?
Yes. A keyword rule can name its own webhook URL. Precedence is the chat-logger keyword URL, then the relay's keywords= route, then the shared webhook. A route on its own is enough.

title: Bridging Discord and Minecraft both ways

messages.content: Can I talk to Minecraft from Discord?

Yes, with tools/discord_bridge.py. It is a separate Python process that talks to the companion API in both directions. It is not part of the mod, because a bot token must not ship inside a client mod and a bot has to stay online when the game is closed.
What do I need?
A Discord bot token, the channel id, and the companion access token from the Companion module. Enable the Message Content intent in the developer portal, or messages arrive with empty text.
Is it safe? Someone in Discord could run commands, right?

Not through the bridge. The companion chat endpoint forwards a message starting with '/' to the command path, which runs it as the player. The bridge strips leading slashes before sending, so `/op Steve` becomes the chat line `op Steve`. A slash mid-sentence is left alone.
And the other direction?

Text from Minecraft is escaped before it reaches Discord: @everyone, @here and role mentions get a zero-width space, and every post pins allowed_mentions to an empty parse list. A player cannot ping a server by typing it in chat.
What stops it from looping forever?

Echo suppression. A Discord message becomes a chat line, which the bridge would otherwise read back and post to Discord again. Injected lines are remembered and consumed, so one injection produces one echo, and a player genuinely repeating the text later still reaches Discord.
Does Log Client record chat by default?
Yes. Recording is on out of the box, so the archive is already there when you first search it. `log record off` stops it.
How do I find something someone said last week?
`log search <terms>`. It searches the recorded archive. `log digest` summarises recent activity and `log timeline` shows joins, leaves and deaths.
Where is the archive stored?
Under the game directory in the Log Client folder. `log status` reports the storage usage, and `log sessions` lists past recording sessions.
What is the companion server?
A small HTTP server inside the client that serves a dashboard and a JSON API, so a phone or another machine can watch and control the bots. It is off by default.
How do I authenticate?
Every request under /api needs the access token, sent as an Authorization Bearer header or a token query parameter. /health and the app shell are open so a browser can load the page.
How do I get live updates?
Subscribe to GET /api/v1/events. It is a server-sent event stream carrying chat, bot and session events. Send Last-Event-ID on reconnect and the server replays what you missed.
Is it safe to expose to my network?

Only if you mean to. It binds to loopback by default and refuses a remote bind without an explicit opt-in, because anyone who can reach the port and has the token can send chat and run commands as you.
What do the Discord messages look like?
They are rich embeds: a coloured card with a title, a description and up to 25 fields, not a wall of text.
My long footer made the card stop appearing. Why?

Discord rejects an embed over 6000 characters across all its parts, and a 400 is not retryable, so the card is dropped rather than delayed. Each part is now clipped against the remaining budget, so the card still sends with the text shortened.
Can I see the card before sending it?
Yes. `log webhook preview` renders it in game, and the embed preview screen shows characters used and remaining against the 6000 budget.
How do I change the colour?
Set the accent setting on the webhook relay. Auto colours each card by its type, or pick a fixed colour.
Nothing reaches Discord.
Check the webhook URL is set and starts with https://discord.com/api/webhooks/. Run `log webhook test` and read the result. `log alerts` shows recent delivery failures.
The bridge connects but Discord messages do nothing.
The Message Content intent is almost certainly off. Without it Discord delivers messages with empty text, so the bridge filters everything out. Enable it in the developer portal and restart the bot.
The bridge says the game did not respond.
That is a 504 from the companion server: the game did not answer within its timeout. It usually means the client is loading, or the main thread is blocked. Try again once you are in a world.
I get 401 from the companion API.
The access token does not match. Copy it again from the Companion module. The token is never logged, so it will not appear in the client log.
